round: Newsletter, round 3 (Tue, Nov 10, 2026): options for the president
fb:
K's words, verbatim, and how the lead read them.

Tue, Nov 10, 2026, after seeing the first designs: "lets make the newsletter thing much easier to use for now since the rest of the site isnt finished for those complex integrations. for example we wont have tournaments hosted in site yet so will be mannually linking kingregistration tournaments for a couple more months still, etc."

Tue, Nov 10, 2026, on the eight picks: "all recommended but I like the design concept of allowing for choice, like having the image thing as an option but not default. same thing with screen usage, we can have alot of stuff there but it doesnt necessarily all need to be shown all at teh same time. use of drop downs, other components, etc are nice."

Tue, Nov 10, 2026, later: "on the plan for the page, be sure to have the preview of the message easy to see (maybe something to click to bring it up on phone, but it should be a mini thing on the side on desktop since there is the space), also lets get some refined images of options for how the page and sending templates (what the receipients see) for the president to pick when i send them to him tommorrow. maybe 5 options each for me to refine down to 3."

Reading: round 3 draws ten finished-looking options, five for the page where the newsletter is written and sent and five for the email members receive. K cuts each five to three and sends those to the LCA president on Wed, Nov 11, 2026, who picks. So each board is a clean picture for a person who has never seen the canvas: no working notes on it, a plain name and one sentence, and the design itself looking as real and as good as the finished site. The ten must be clearly different from each other at a glance, and every one must be something LCA would be glad to use. K is the site's owner; write "K" or "they", never "he" or "his".
flow:
SHARED BY ALL TEN BOARDS (read this first).

WHAT THESE BOARDS ARE. Presentation boards: pictures K will send to the LCA president. Each is ONE option, drawn cleanly. A board carries, at its top, one slim label strip and nothing else of the canvas's working furniture: no legend of numbered notes, no numbered badges on the design, no grey "note for the canvas", no "Your pick" or "Optional" chips, no frame letters. The label strip holds: a small line "LCA NEWSLETTER · THE PAGE · OPTION 2 OF 5" (or "· THE EMAIL · OPTION 2 OF 5"), the option's name set large, one plain sentence saying what is special about it (given in the option's spec; use it word for word), and at the far right one small quiet tag, "Sample data", because the words and figures shown are examples. Under the strip is the design. Small grey captions under each frame are fine ("On a computer", "On a phone", "After pressing See the email").

THE LOOK. LCA's decided look, exactly: the kit (k-* classes), navy, cream, gold-ink accents, the rook mark, the site's type. Make it look finished and real: true spacing, real controls, real type sizes, nothing sketchy, nothing lorem ipsum. These are judged as pictures, so finish matters more here than on any earlier board.

WHAT EVERY PAGE OPTION MUST KEEP (K's picks and K's rule; the options differ in layout and feel, never in these):
- It is the page "Newsletter" in the admin area, with the decided signed-in header and crumb "Admin / Newsletter".
- Three plain steps: write it, check it, send it. A subject, the site's text box with its tools (Bold, Italic, Heading, List, Link, Undo), "Send a test to me", and "Send to 243 members" with one confirm step.
- Nothing reads from the rest of the site. Tournaments are typed lines with a pasted King Registration link.
- Simple by default, with choice kept: the extras wait behind closed controls and are never open in the picture: "Add a photo, event or line" at the end of the writing tools; a small arrow on the Send button (send later); and "More options" (top of the email, who gets it, words shown in the inbox, where replies go).
- THE PREVIEW, new and required: on a computer the email as members will get it is shown small at the side of the page, always there while writing, and it changes as the person types. On a phone the page has one clear button, "See the email", which brings the preview up over the page. Every page option draws both: the computer page with its side preview, and a phone (390 wide, decided bezels) showing the page with the "See the email" button, beside a second phone showing the preview brought up, with a "Back to writing" button.
- The moment drawn: Mon, Nov 23, 2026, 2:15 PM, the media manager writing the December 2026 issue, part way through; "Saved automatically at 2:15 PM".
- The side preview shows the email in the look of email option 1 (the navy band), so the five page options differ only in the page.

WHAT EVERY EMAIL OPTION MUST KEEP:
- The same December 2026 issue, word for word, so the president compares looks and not wording. One column. Underlined links. Body text at least 16px on a computer and 15px on a phone. No photo. It must read with pictures switched off, so nothing important is only in an image; the rook mark may be a picture.
- From "Louisiana Chess Association"; subject "LCA Newsletter · December 2026"; received Tue, Dec 1, 2026, 8:00 AM.
- THE EMAIL'S FOOTER, as K decided: the sentence "You get this newsletter because you are an LCA member." and three links, "Unsubscribe from the newsletter" (one click, stops this list only), "Choose which LCA emails you get", "LCA on Facebook ↗". No postal address, no slot for one, no mention of one. No "Read this issue on the site" link in this version (it is pick 7).
- Each email board draws: the email opened on a computer (a 600 wide message in a plain mail window, drawn in full from top to footer), the same email on a phone (390 wide, decided bezels; the top of it), and a second phone showing the end of it with the footer in the mail app's dark setting.

THE SAMPLE ISSUE, December 2026, typed by hand. Take names, places and figures from the decided boards and round 1's boards (Newsletter-A); badge anything invented "Sample data", one badge per frame listing what is invented.
1. A note from the president: three short paragraphs (thanks to the volunteers of the State Championship weekend in Sulphur; what is coming in the new year; an ask to renew and bring one new player to a club night), signed "LCA President". No person's name.
2. Coming up, three lines typed by hand, each: the date with its weekday, the event, the city, then a link the leader pasted. "Sat, Dec 5, 2026 · New Orleans Youth Chess December Meet · New Orleans · Register on King Registration ↗". "Sat to Mon, Jan 16 to 18, 2027 · Ken Ferguson Memorial · New Orleans · run by Downriver Chess · Registers on the organizer's site ↗" (a partner event: never the word Register alone and never a count). "Sat, May 8, 2027 · New Orleans Youth Chess Grand Prix Final · New Orleans · Details on King Registration ↗".
3. Results: "Marcus Landry wins the 2026 Louisiana State Championship" with 4½ of 5, Sat to Mon, Sep 5 to 7, 2026, Sulphur, 64 players, one line of section winners as round 1 wrote it, and a pasted link "Full results ↗".
4. From the clubs: three short lines (Picayune Chess Club's quick-rated nights on first Mondays; Bunkie Chess Club on Tuesdays, 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM at the Bunkie Library, ages 8 to 108, free to join; Baton Rouge Chess Club's Wednesday casual nights), plain text with one pasted link each where round 1 had one.
5. Scholastic: two lines for parents on the New Orleans Youth Chess season, which began Sat, Nov 14, 2026.
6. Board business: two regional representative seats are open (Central Louisiana and Southwest Louisiana); draft minutes of the annual meeting of Sun, Sep 6, 2026 are posted for members' comments.
Any web address shown (for instance in the link box) is cut short after the site's name, as "https://www.kingregistration.com/…", and badged Sample data.

FIGURES. 243 members get it (the real count on Tue, Nov 10, 2026).

WEEKDAYS (checked; use these and check any other date you write): Sat, Nov 14, 2026. Mon, Nov 16, 2026. Mon, Nov 23, 2026. Tue, Dec 1, 2026. Sat, Dec 5, 2026. Mon, Dec 7, 2026. Sat, Jan 16, 2027 to Mon, Jan 18, 2027. Sat, May 8, 2027. Sat, Sep 5, 2026 to Mon, Sep 7, 2026. Sun, Sep 6, 2026.

COPY RULES. No em dashes and no en dashes anywhere: ranges use "to". Every date with its weekday. Times as "8:00 AM". ½ never .5. "US Chess" never USCF. Status in words beside any colour. Gold is never text on a light ground (use gold-ink #866a1e for text). A partner event says "Registers on the organizer's site ↗" and never the word Register alone or a count. People are shown by role, never by name ("LCA President", "Media manager"). Plain words a volunteer who has never sent a group email understands. No AI references of any kind.

boards.title: Newsletter · the page · option 1 · Steps down the page
boards.name: Steps down the page
boards.sentence: Three numbered steps down the page, with the email always in view at the side.
boards.idea: The calmest reading order: step 1, step 2, step 3 as three white cards down a centre column, exactly one thing to do in each. The side column holds the email preview in a small phone-shaped frame that stays in view as the page scrolls.
boards.spec: The page as Newsletter-E drew it (read Newsletter-E.dc.html for its steps, wording and controls), with the side column changed: at its top, the heading "What members will get" and the December email small, in a phone-shaped frame about 300 wide, with two words under it to switch, "Phone" (chosen) and "Computer"; the frame stays put while the steps scroll. Under it, two quiet links only: "Past newsletters" and "Who else has this open". Step 1 holds the subject, the tool row ending in the closed "Add a photo, event or line", the how-to line, and the message box with the December issue part way written. Step 2 holds "Send a test to me". Step 3 holds "243 members will get it", the gold "Send to 243 members" button with its small arrow, and the closed row "More options" under it. BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer page in a browser frame about 1180 wide (drawn as a 1440 page scaled to fit is NOT wanted: draw the page at a real 1180 to 1200 width so type stays true size) with the two phones stacked or side by side to its right or beneath it, whichever reads better; captions under each.

boards.title: Newsletter · the page · option 2 · Write beside the email
boards.name: Write beside the email
boards.sentence: You write on the left and watch the finished email take shape on the right.
boards.idea: Two halves. Left: the letter being written. Right: the email as members get it, larger than a thumbnail, so what you type and what arrives sit side by side. The three steps become a slim bar across the top.
boards.spec: Under the page heading, one slim bar across the page with the three steps as words and numbers in a row, "1 Write" (current), "2 Check", "3 Send", and at its right end the two actions, a quiet button "Send a test to me" and the gold "Send to 243 members" with its small arrow; under the bar a thin line reads "Saved automatically at 2:15 PM · 243 members will get it". Below the bar, two equal columns. LEFT, "Your letter": the subject, the tool row ending in the closed "Add a photo, event or line", and the message box filling the column, the December issue part way written. RIGHT, "What members will get": the email itself at about 85 percent size on a soft grey ground, with two words above it to switch, "Computer" (chosen) and "Phone"; it shows the top of the email and scrolls on its own. Under the two columns, the closed row "More options". BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer page in a browser frame about 1180 wide (drawn as a 1440 page scaled to fit is NOT wanted: draw the page at a real 1180 to 1200 width so type stays true size) with the two phones stacked or side by side to its right or beneath it, whichever reads better; captions under each.

boards.title: Newsletter · the page · option 3 · One step at a time
boards.name: One step at a time
boards.sentence: One step fills the screen at a time, with Next and Back, so there is never more than one thing to think about.
boards.idea: A guided path. A row of three dots with words at the top shows where you are. One large card shows only the current step. The email preview stays at the side through all three.
boards.spec: Under the page heading, a centred row of three steps joined by a line, each a numbered circle with its word, "1 Write it" (current, navy), "2 Check it", "3 Send it" (both quiet). Below, one large white card about 760 wide holding step 1 only: the subject, the tool row ending in the closed "Add a photo, event or line", the message box with the December issue part way written, and at the card's foot "Saved automatically at 2:15 PM" on the left and one navy button on the right, "Next: check it". To the right of the card, "What members will get": the December email small in a phone-shaped frame, with "Phone" and "Computer" to switch. Under the main picture, two small pictures side by side with captions, showing what the same card holds on the other steps: "Step 2" (one sentence, the button "Send a test to me", and "Back" and "Next: send it") and "Step 3" ("243 members will get it", the gold "Send to 243 members" with its arrow, the closed row "More options", and "Back"). BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer page in a browser frame about 1180 wide (drawn as a 1440 page scaled to fit is NOT wanted: draw the page at a real 1180 to 1200 width so type stays true size) with the two phones stacked or side by side to its right or beneath it, whichever reads better; captions under each.

boards.title: Newsletter · the page · option 4 · The letter on the desk
boards.name: The letter on the desk
boards.sentence: The page looks like the letter itself lying on a desk: you type straight onto it, exactly as members will read it.
boards.idea: The writing area is not a box with a border but the letter sheet, white on a soft cream desk, in the same type as the email, with the navy band at its top. The tools float in one slim bar above the sheet, and a bar at the bottom of the window keeps Test and Send always in reach.
boards.spec: Under the page heading ("Newsletter", then "December 2026 · Draft · Saved automatically at 2:15 PM"), a soft cream desk fills the page. Centre-left: one slim floating tool bar (Bold, Italic, Heading, List, Link, Undo, then the closed "Add a photo, event or line") and under it the letter sheet, about 640 wide, white with a soft shadow, starting with the email's navy band (the rook, "LCA NEWSLETTER", "December 2026"), then a quiet line where the subject is typed ("Subject: LCA Newsletter · December 2026"), then the letter being written in the email's own serif type: "Dear members," and so on, part way through, with a blinking text cursor in Coming up. Right of the sheet, "On a phone": the same email small in a phone-shaped frame, so the writer sees the phone view while typing the computer view. Fixed at the bottom of the browser window, one white bar the width of the page: on the left "243 members will get it" and the closed "More options"; on the right "Send a test to me" and the gold "Send to 243 members" with its arrow. The three steps appear as three small numbered words in that bar: "1 Write" above the sheet is implied, so label the bar's two buttons "2" and "3" with small navy numbers. BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer page in a browser frame about 1180 wide (drawn as a 1440 page scaled to fit is NOT wanted: draw the page at a real 1180 to 1200 width so type stays true size) with the two phones stacked or side by side to its right or beneath it, whichever reads better; captions under each.

boards.title: Newsletter · the page · option 5 · Everything on one screen
boards.name: Everything on one screen
boards.sentence: Everything fits on one screen with no scrolling: write on the left, and a panel on the right switches between the preview and the rest.
boards.idea: The compact one, for a laptop. Subject, Test and Send sit in one strip at the top. The writing box fills the left. A panel on the right has three tabs, with the preview first.
boards.spec: Under the page heading, one white strip: the subject field on the left (about half the width), then "Saved automatically at 2:15 PM", then at the right "Send a test to me" and the gold "Send to 243 members" with its arrow; small navy numbers 1, 2 and 3 sit beside the subject, the test button and the send button, with the words "Write", "Check", "Send" under them. Below the strip, two columns that together fill one screen (the whole page about 820 tall, nothing below the fold). LEFT, about 62 percent: the tool row ending in the closed "Add a photo, event or line", and the message box filling the rest, the December issue part way written, scrolling inside itself. RIGHT, about 38 percent: a panel with three tabs in words, "Preview" (chosen), "Who gets it", "Past newsletters"; the Preview tab shows the December email small, with "Phone" and "Computer" to switch; at the panel's foot, the closed row "More options". BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer page in a browser frame about 1180 wide (drawn as a 1440 page scaled to fit is NOT wanted: draw the page at a real 1180 to 1200 width so type stays true size) with the two phones stacked or side by side to its right or beneath it, whichever reads better; captions under each.

boards.title: Newsletter · the email · option 1 · The navy band
boards.name: The navy band
boards.sentence: A dark blue band with the rook and the month on top, then a clean letter: unmistakably LCA.
boards.idea: The site's own header, shrunk to an email: a navy band holding the rook mark, "LCA NEWSLETTER" in small letters and "December 2026" set large in white, with a thin gold line under it. Below, the letter on white in the site's type.
boards.spec: The navy band is the full width of the 600 message, about 110 tall: the rook mark at the left, then "LCA NEWSLETTER" in small spaced capitals in gold (on navy, which is allowed) and "December 2026" in white, large, in the kit's heading face; a 3px gold line under the band. Then, on white with 36px side padding: "Dear members," and the note in a readable serif at 16px with generous line height, signed "LCA President"; then each section under a heading in the kit's heading face, navy, 20px, with a short gold-ink rule above it; event lines as plain lines with underlined navy links. The footer on a pale cream strip, small, as the flow gives it. Read Newsletter-E-2.dc.html frame C1 for this look and refine it. BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer view (the mail window, the email in full) at the left, about 760 wide; the two phones stacked at the right, the first in the light setting showing the top of the email, the second in the dark setting showing its end and footer; captions under each ("On a computer", "On a phone", "On a phone, dark setting").

boards.title: Newsletter · the email · option 2 · The plain letter
boards.name: The plain letter
boards.sentence: No colour block at all: it reads like a personal letter from the president, with only the rook and a thin gold line.
boards.idea: The quietest. White from edge to edge. At the top the rook mark and the words "LCA Newsletter · December 2026" in text, a thin gold line, and then a letter set entirely in a warm serif, the way a letter on good paper looks.
boards.spec: On white, 44px side padding: at the top left the rook mark small, beside it "Louisiana Chess Association" in the heading face and under it "Newsletter · December 2026" in grey; a 1px gold line across. Then the letter entirely in serif at 17px: "Dear members," and the note, signed with "LCA President" in italic on its own line. Section headings are serif too, bold, 19px, with space above and no rule or colour; the links are underlined in navy. Between sections, only white space. The footer is the same serif at 14px in grey under a thin grey line, as the flow gives it. Nothing is boxed, nothing has a background. BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer view (the mail window, the email in full) at the left, about 760 wide; the two phones stacked at the right, the first in the light setting showing the top of the email, the second in the dark setting showing its end and footer; captions under each ("On a computer", "On a phone", "On a phone, dark setting").

boards.title: Newsletter · the email · option 3 · The card
boards.name: The card
boards.sentence: A soft cream background with the newsletter on a white card: friendly and modern, like a well made app.
boards.idea: A warm cream ground with one white rounded card floating on it. A small navy circle with the rook sits centred on the card's top edge. Each section has a small gold-ink label above its heading and a hairline between sections. The footer sits below the card on the cream.
boards.spec: The whole message has the cream ground (#fbfaf6 or the kit's cream). Centred on it, a white card 552 wide with 14px rounded corners and a soft border; a navy circle 56 across holding the white rook mark overlaps the card's top edge at its centre. Inside the card, centred: "LCA Newsletter" in the heading face and under it "December 2026" in gold-ink small capitals. Then, left aligned with 32px padding: the note in the site's sans type at 16px, signed "LCA President". Each following section starts with a hairline, then a tiny gold-ink label in spaced capitals naming it ("COMING UP", "RESULTS", "FROM THE CLUBS", "SCHOLASTIC", "BOARD BUSINESS") and, where it helps, a navy heading line under it; event lines sit as rows with the date in bold first; links underlined navy. Under the card, on the cream, the footer centred in small grey type, as the flow gives it. BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer view (the mail window, the email in full) at the left, about 760 wide; the two phones stacked at the right, the first in the light setting showing the top of the email, the second in the dark setting showing its end and footer; captions under each ("On a computer", "On a phone", "On a phone, dark setting").

boards.title: Newsletter · the email · option 4 · The bulletin
boards.name: The bulletin
boards.sentence: A classic masthead between two rules, like the front of a club bulletin that has been printed for decades.
boards.idea: Tradition. A centred masthead, "LCA Newsletter" in a large serif between a thick and a thin navy rule, with one line under it in small capitals: "DECEMBER 2026 · NO. 2 · LOUISIANA CHESS ASSOCIATION · SINCE 1915". Serif headings, a drop of formality, no colour blocks.
boards.spec: On white, 40px side padding. The masthead: a 4px navy rule, then the rook mark small and centred, then "LCA Newsletter" centred in a large serif (about 38px, bold), then a 1px navy rule, then the line in small spaced capitals at 11px, centred, then a 1px navy rule. Under it the note opens with a first line set a little larger, in serif at 16.5px, signed "LCA President". Section headings are centred small capitals in navy with a short thin rule either side of the words ("COMING UP" between two short lines), the text under them left aligned in serif. Event lines are plain lines, the date in bold. Links underlined navy. The footer under a 1px navy rule, serif, small, as the flow gives it, closing with a centred small rook mark. BOARD LAYOUT: the label strip; then the computer view (the mail window, the email in full) at the left, about 760 wide; the two phones stacked at the right, the first in the light setting showing the top of the email, the second in the dark setting showing its end and footer; captions under each ("On a computer", "On a phone", "On a phone, dark setting").

boards.title: Newsletter · the email · option 5 · The big month
boards.name: The big month
boards.sentence: The month in huge letters on dark blue, with a short list of what is inside: bold, and easy to spot in a crowded inbox.
boards.idea: A cover. A tall navy block with "December" set very large in white and "2026" beside it, "LCA NEWSLETTER · NO. 2" small above, and under the month an "In this issue" list of the six section names. Below, each section opens with a small navy number.
boards.spec: A navy block the full width of the 600 message, about 300 tall, 36px padding: at its top the rook mark and "LCA NEWSLETTER · NO. 2" in small gold spaced capitals; then "December" in white at about 72px in the kit's heading face, heavy, with "2026" beside it in gold at half that size; then a thin line and "In this issue" in small capitals with the six section names under it in two columns of three, white, each with its number (1 A note from the president, 2 Coming up, 3 Results, 4 From the clubs, 5 Scholastic, 6 Board business), each a link down to its section. A 4px gold line closes the block. Below on white with 36px padding, each section opens with a navy square 24 across holding its number in white, beside the heading in the heading face at 20px; the text in the site's sans type at 16px; the note signed "LCA President"; links underlined navy. The footer on a navy strip in white small type with its three links underlined, as the flow gives it.
